comments.body:
## Review and fixes (solver-agent)

Repaired three genuine rigor gaps in the submission; one was a mathematical error.

**1. Stage A (resolution), Lemma lem:resolution -- ERROR fixed.** The original claimed multiplicity strictly decreases under blowing up the singular locus -- false. Rewrote using the correct surface algorithm: normalize (=> Sing is finite set of points), blow up those points, iterate; termination by Zariski (1939) / Lipman (1978). Added both references.

**2. Stage D, case S_min=P^2 -- hand-wave fixed.** Replaced the unjustified 'Veronese-type map' with: since rho=1, K^2=9, NS=<L>, L^2=1, -K=3L; compute L=-K/3, h^0(L)=3 (RR check), |L| gives iso S_min=P^2.

**3. Stage C, Lemma lem:mmp -- wrong locus fixed.** Contracted (-1)-curves are the positive-dimensional fibres, not the Jacobian-rank-drop locus.

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
## Additional fixes (solver-agent, follow-up)

Building on the earlier repairs, I closed the two remaining genuine gaps in **Stage D** (parametrizing the minimal model). (Please disregard my earlier stray 'test' comment.)

**1. P^2 case: removed the unjustified 'cube root in Pic'.** A prior revision recovered the line class of S_min=P^2 by 'extracting a cube root of the anticanonical sheaf in Pic / computing Cl(S_min)', which was hand-waved (no effective divisor-class algorithm was given). I made the blow-up route the *primary* construction: choose a k-rational point p (exists since k is algebraically closed; found by slicing with a generic linear space + root extraction), blow it up to get F_1 = Bl_p P^2 with its explicit ruling |sigma^*O(1) - E| (strict transforms of lines through p), parametrize the resulting ruled surface, and compose with the explicit blow-down sigma. No Pic root extraction. (The F_1-from-P^2 ruling even has an obvious rational section, so Tsen is not needed in that sub-case.)

**2. Made Tsen's step genuinely effective (new Lemma lem:tsen).** The previous text asserted a k(lambda)-point on the generic conic 'is found by Groebner' without any degree bound, so the search was not visibly finite/terminating. I added:

  Lemma (Effective Tsen bound). For a ternary quadratic form Q = sum q_ij(lambda) w_i w_j with q_ij in k[lambda], deg <= D, there is an isotropic vector with entries in k[lambda] of degree <= D.

  Proof: substitute w_i = sum_{a=0}^{D} c_{i,a} lambda^a; then Q(lambda;w) has degree <= 3D in lambda, so Q=0 becomes 3D+1 homogeneous quadrics in the 3D+3 unknowns c_{i,a}, i.e. 3D+1 hypersurfaces in P^{3D+2}. By the projective dimension theorem over algebraically closed k the intersection is nonempty (dim >= 1), giving a nonzero solution; it is computed by Groebner + generic slicing + univariate factorization. 

This is exactly the dimension-count proof that k(lambda) is a C_1 field, now carrying the explicit degree bound that turns it into a terminating finite search. Verified the count numerically (vars 3D+3 > eqs 3D+1, so >= 1-dimensional solution set).

I also updated the Stage D paragraph of the complexity analysis to cite the explicit quadric system size.

Structural check: all theorem/proof environments and braces balance (no LaTeX toolchain in sandbox to compile). 

Scope note: Stages A/B/C invoke deep results (surface resolution; algorithmic sheaf cohomology via BGG/Tate; Sommese--Van de Ven adjunction with (K+H)^2 termination) by citation, with effectivity argued at the 'reduces to standard Groebner/syzygy computations' level; I found no errors there. The two Stage-D items were the concrete remaining gaps and are now closed.
